title: Do line-specific pictures improve visual timing review?
scope: Two public Tears of Steel excerpts in English. The opening has one original and one edited narration. Fixed annotations cover visual grounding and timing. These are selected examples.

decisionEvidence.reviewCriterion: Require a spoiler violation on opening L6 with stills and zero spoiler or unseen violations on accepted lines in every still-assisted review.
reviewFindings: Opening L6 was flagged as a spoiler with and without stills.
The still-assisted check rejected opening L2 as a spoiler in both versions. These two judgments concern identical words and pictures.
decisionEvidence.blindCriterion: Compare each anonymous judgment to the frozen visual label. Later and not_visible reject a line. An indeterminate judgment remains unresolved.

reasonAlignmentNotes.B3: The line-level rejection agrees with the frozen label. The label questions whether the object can be identified as a microphone. The model called it a microphone and rejected the timing of the raising action.
reasonAlignmentNotes.B1: The frozen label questions when the arm goes around the other man. The blind answer also disputes the timing of pointing. The earlier general review cited the pronoun and the spelling of the name.
reasonAlignmentNotes.A1: The blind answer disputes the onset of ascent. It recognizes the exhaust at the opening.
reasonAlignmentNotes.B2: The blind answer recognizes the transforming grid at the opening and disputes when the sunny town becomes visible.

blindTimingCall.deduplication: Five unchanged opening lines shared identical wording, start and end times, and frame evidence across the original and edited runs. Each appears once in this call.
blindTimingCall.systemInstruction:
For each narration line, identify the visible subject, action or change its wording claims at the stated start. The clip letter on a line identifies its video; each clip has its own clock. Decide each line independently.
Use the labeled opening and ending pictures and the moving clip. The opening picture was sampled after the line started. If a cut or reveal occurs between the stated start and that picture, consult the moving clip. When the timing cannot be resolved, return indeterminate.
Use supported when the claim is visually supported by the time narration begins. Use later when a detail is first shown after that time. Use not_visible when the claim lacks visual support throughout the clip. When several details are claimed, quote the specific words that determine your judgment. Note what is actually visible in the opening picture and later in the clip. Do not infer exact onset times from the stills. Ignore style, script coverage and audio quality. Return one judgment for each listed line ID.
blindTimingCall.observations: quotedWords, openingObservation, laterObservation, firstSeenIn and status are the returned model fields. Any onset times within observation text are model estimates.
